applies_why: The judge text rules D6 vs C4 UNDERDETERMINED, so the rule governing grounds for UNDERDETERMINED applies.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: the phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary'; I weighed whether it forbids any UNDERDETERMINED resting on a verse's silence versus whether a ruling resting on the defender having dropped the pressed limb is a different, procedural ground.
why: The judge does not rest on Jeremiah 22:30 failing to state the link or contrary; it rests on the curse limb having been dropped, leaving no live link to contradict.
